steps.body: A ruler measures by marks: an object from the 3 cm mark to the 11 cm mark is 11 − 3 = 8 cm — the END mark is not the length.
steps.narration: A ruler measures by marks: an object from the 3 cm mark to the 11 cm mark is 11 − 3 = 8 cm — the END mark is not the length.

widget.prompt: Measure the ribbon with one-unit blocks: align its start, place four with no gaps or overlaps.
widget.successFeedback: Four one-unit blocks tile the ribbon exactly — the count of units IS the length, wherever the ribbon starts.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: An object runs from mark 3 to mark 11. Is it 11 cm long?
predict.reveal: The stretch before mark 3 belongs to the ruler, not the object; subtracting the start returns the true 8.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2p length diff.
invariants: Lengths compare only from a shared start, join by placing end to end, and split so the parts rebuild the whole exactly for g2p length diff.
misconceptions: Comparing unaligned ends, reading a ruler's end mark as a length, or letting a total drift from the sum of its parts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to change about the pieces for the total or the gap to come out differently?

widget.prompt: A pencil stretches from the 2 cm mark to the 9 cm mark on a ruler. How long is it?

commonErrors.feedback: That read the END mark as the length — a start away from zero must be subtracted off.
Adding the marks measures nothing on a ruler; the length is the span BETWEEN them.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the lengths up: same starting point, then read what the ends say — joins add, gaps subtract.

hints: The length is the span between.

widget.prompt: Two trail legs of 32 m and 25 m give a computed total of 30 m. Reasonable?

options.label: Impossible — a total cannot be shorter than one of its parts
options.feedback: Correct — joining 32 with anything positive lands past 32; a 30 m total contradicts its own first leg.

options.label: Reasonable — totals vary
options.feedback: Totals obey their parts: 32 + 25 must reach 57, never dip below 32.

options.label: Reasonable if the legs overlap
options.feedback: Trail legs walked one after another do not overlap — each adds its full distance.

options.label: Only a ruler could tell
options.feedback: Sense-checking needs no tools here — part-vs-total logic already rules 30 out.
